description:
Text to speech (TTS) lets Wynem read messages out loud. Join a voice channel and use the <command:tts [text]|voice tts message:[text]> command, and Wynem will join your voice channel and speak your message.

If you are not in a voice channel, or you use the command in Wynem's direct messages, the message is sent as an `mp3` file instead.

data.name: Ewan
data.message: e!tts Hello everyone, welcome to the server!

description: Wynem reacts to your message once it starts reading it out. When using the slash command, Wynem instead replies with the message being read out:

components: **<@Ewan>:** Hello everyone, welcome to the server!

description: Before a message is read out, Wynem cleans it up so that it sounds natural when spoken:

rows: User, channel, and role mentions are read out as their names
Links are read out as just the website name
Very long numbers, such as Discord IDs, are skipped
Common abbreviations are expanded, such as `btw` becoming `by the way` and `brb` becoming `be right back`
Fully censored words like `****` are swapped for random words, and `*`s inside words are replaced with random vowels

description: Messages can be up to `1000` characters long after processing. Anything longer will not be read out.

description:
To read a single message in another language, put the language inside square brackets at the start of your message.
For example: <command:tts [fr] Bonjour!|voice tts message:Bonjour! language:French>

To change your default TTS language, use the <command:setttslanguage [language]|voice setttslanguage language:[language]> command. Your language is saved to you, and is used everywhere, including AutoTTS.
Setting your language to `en` or `en-uk` resets it back to the default. Running the command without a language shows all the available languages, along with your current one.

tabs.name: Changing the volume
content: To change how loud Wynem speaks, use the <command:volume [volume]|voice volume volume:[volume]> command with a volume between `1` and `100`. You must be in the same voice channel as Wynem to change the volume.
For example: e!volume 50/voice volume volume:50

author: Voice volume set
/assets/images/icons/speaker_blue.webp
data.description: My volume has been set to 50%

content: If Wynem is already reading something out, the new volume is applied after the current playback finishes.
Running the command without a volume shows the current volume.

author: Voice volume

data.description: My voice volume is currently set to 50%

tabs.name: Setting the default volume
content: The default volume is the volume Wynem starts at whenever it joins a voice channel in your server. It defaults to `100`%.
To change it, use the `e!defaultvolume [volume]` command with a volume between `1` and `100`. This command requires the `Manage Server` permission, and is only available as a prefix command.
For example: `e!defaultvolume 75`

/assets/images/icons/speaker_blue.webp
data.description: My default volume has been set to 75%

content: If Wynem is currently in a voice channel, the new default volume is used the next time it joins one.
Running the command without a volume shows the current default volume.

tabs.name: Stopping and leaving
content: To make Wynem stop reading the current message, use the <command:stop|voice stop> command. Wynem reacts with a 🛑 once the audio has been stopped.
To make Wynem leave the voice channel entirely, use the <command:leave|voice leave> command. Wynem reacts with a 👋 as it leaves.
You must be in the same voice channel as Wynem to use either command.

description: AutoTTS turns a channel into a hands free TTS channel: every message sent in it is automatically read out loud in your voice channel, with no command needed. Messages are processed and spoken exactly like the <command:tts [text]|voice tts message:[text]> command, using each member's own TTS language.
A message in the AutoTTS channel is only read out if:

rows: You are in a voice channel
Messages are not read for members who are not in a voice channel
Messages starting with the server's prefix, or any of the ignored prefixes, are skipped
Messages that are just a link are skipped
It is not from a bot
Bot messages are never read out

tabs.name: Setting the AutoTTS channel
content: Setting up AutoTTS requires the `Manage Server` permission.
To set the AutoTTS channel, use the <command:setautotts [channel]|serverconfig autotts set channel:[channel]> command. The channel is optional, and defaults to the channel the command is run in.
For example: e!setautotts #autotts/serverconfig autotts set channel:#autotts

data.title: AutoTTS channel set
data.description: The AutoTTS channel has been set to <#autotts>

content: A server can only have one AutoTTS channel at a time. Running the command again moves the AutoTTS to the new channel.

tabs.name: Viewing the AutoTTS channel
content: To see which channel is currently the AutoTTS channel, use the <command:viewautotts|voice viewautotts> command.
If no AutoTTS channel is set, you will get an error instead.

author: Error
/assets/images/icons/error.webp
data.title: No AutoTTS channel set
data.description: There is no AutoTTS channel set in this server

tabs.name: Ignoring prefixes
content: If you use other bots in the AutoTTS channel, you can stop their commands being read out loud by ignoring their prefixes. This requires the `Manage Server` permission.

To ignore a prefix, use the <command:ignoreprefix [prefix]|serverconfig autotts ignoreprefix prefix:[prefix]> command.
For example: <command:ignoreprefix !|serverconfig autotts ignoreprefix prefix:!>

data.title: Prefix ignored
data.description: The prefix `!` will be ignored for AutoTTS

content: Up to `10` prefixes can be ignored at a time. Wynem's own prefix is always ignored automatically.
Running the command with a prefix that is already ignored removes it from the ignored prefixes.

data.title: Prefix no longer ignored
data.description: The prefix `!` is no longer ignored for AutoTTS

content: Running the command without a prefix shows the currently ignored prefixes.

data.title: Ignored AutoTTS prefixes
data.description:
`!`, `?`

You can add more ignored prefixes with the `e!ignoreprefix [prefix]` command

tabs.name: Removing the AutoTTS channel
content: To remove the AutoTTS channel, use the <command:removeautotts|serverconfig autotts remove> command. This requires the `Manage Server` permission.
You will be prompted to confirm you want to remove the AutoTTS

data.description: Are you sure you want to remove the AutoTTS from <#autotts>?

content: After confirming, the AutoTTS channel will have been removed.

data.title: AutoTTS removed
